title: Restaurant POS vs patchwork tools: why one spine wins on a busy night
description: How restaurants lose covers when till, kitchen tickets, and bookings live in separate apps — and what a unified hospitality ops platform changes on the floor.
body:
On a peak Friday, the patchwork shows. Orders in one app. Kitchen tickets on paper or a second screen. Bookings bolted on from a widget. Supervisors chasing deletes in a spreadsheet.

Hostora is built as one operational spine for hospitality — till, kitchen display, guest QR, payments, stock, and staff — so the floor stays aligned under load.

What breaks with patchwork

  • Kitchen stations miss modifiers and notes
  • Takeaway and table service fight over the same stock
  • Supervisors cannot see deletions and stalls live

What “one spine” means

Orders flow from till or guest QR into kitchen display and thermal printers by station. Payments and sales reports sit on the same night. Optional hardware — local Docker server with PostgreSQL, tills, tablets, printers — keeps devices online on your venue network.

Who Hostora is for

Restaurants, takeaways, event venues, hotel F&B outlets (not hotel room PMS), and food carts across the US, UK and Europe.
